findings.highlight: I’ll go home for now.
findings.evidenceJa: とりあえず戻ろう。
findings.governingReading: Shirou decides to head back for the moment and ask Taiga what she knows about Ayako.
findings.explanation: “Go home” fixes the destination where 戻ろう only says return; home is likely but remains inferred through Taiga.

findings.highlight: The sun is setting
findings.evidenceJa: 夕日は地平線に沈みはじめ
findings.governingReading: The evening sun has begun sinking beneath the horizon.
findings.explanation: The English removes the horizon and the onset of descent, weakening the concrete clock-like sunset staging used to estimate darkness in an hour.

findings.highlight: I get to the stairs. As I start walking down, I hear a sound above my head.
findings.evidenceJa: 三階の階段に着く。鞄をぶら下げて帰路につこうとしたその時、かたん、と頭上で物音がした。
findings.governingReading: At the third-floor stairs, just as Shirou hangs his bag at his side and starts home, a small clatter sounds overhead.
findings.explanation: The English omits the floor, bag posture, and concrete sound, then invents that he has started walking downward; these details establish his exact position beneath Rin.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka is standing at the top of the stairs.
findings.evidenceJa: 四階に続く踊り場で仁王立ちしている、遠坂の姿があった。
findings.governingReading: Rin stands planted imposingly on the landing leading to the fourth floor.
findings.explanation: “Top of the stairs” removes the fourth-floor destination, landing, and 仁王立ち’s confrontational wide-planted stance, flattening the visual power imbalance.

findings.highlight: I can’t turn Saber into spirit form
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは霊体化できないんだから
findings.governingReading: Saber is herself unable to assume spirit form.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the transformation to Shirou’s power over Saber, implying he cannot turn her incorporeal rather than stating her unusual inherent limitation.

findings.highlight: if a Master is walking without its Servant
findings.evidenceJa: マスターがサーヴァント抜きでのこのこ歩いてるなんて
findings.governingReading: A Master strolling around blithely or vulnerably without a Servant is effectively asking to be killed.
findings.explanation: The English drops のこのこ, Rin’s contemptuous description of Shirou wandering casually into danger, weakening her anger and concern.

findings.highlight: a Master is walking without its Servant
findings.evidenceJa: マスターがサーヴァント抜きでのこのこ歩いてるなんて
findings.governingReading: A human Master walks without his or her Servant.
findings.explanation: The English uses “its” for the human Master, producing a dehumanizing or agreement error in a basic relationship explanation.

findings.highlight: I bet there are only teachers remaining on the first floor
findings.evidenceJa: 一階にしか生徒や教師は残っていないのではないだろうか
findings.governingReading: Shirou conjectures that any remaining students or teachers may now be confined to the first floor.
findings.explanation: The English omits students and leaves only teachers, changing who may interrupt the fight while retaining the floor inference.

findings.highlight: I told you so many times
findings.evidenceJa: あれだけ教えてあげたのに
findings.governingReading: Despite everything Rin explained or taught him, he has walked into danger himself.
findings.explanation: “So many times” changes あれだけ’s amount and extent of instruction into repeated occasions, overstating how often Rin warned him.

findings.highlight: Saying so angrily
findings.evidenceJa: 棘のある口調で言いながら
findings.governingReading: Rin speaks in a barbed, needling tone as she rolls up her sleeve.
findings.explanation: “Angrily” names general emotion but loses the pointed verbal sharpness that coexists with her controlled, emotionless threat.

findings.highlight: it must be the proof of a magus, a Magic Crest.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師の証と言われる魔術刻印ではないのか。
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether the mark might be the Magic Crest said to signify a magus.
findings.explanation: “It must be” promotes his tentative recognition into certainty and sits awkwardly after the preceding “Could that be,” blurring the discovery sequence.

findings.highlight: a crystallization of the magic passed down my family.
findings.evidenceJa: わたしの家に伝わる魔術の結晶よ。
findings.governingReading: Rin calls the crest the crystallization of magecraft transmitted through her family.
findings.explanation: “Passed down my family” is missing the necessary “in” or “through” and uses generic magic for 魔術, marring a central inheritance explanation.

findings.highlight: ‘Gandr Shot’
findings.evidenceJa: “ガンド撃ち”
findings.governingReading: Rin names the Gandr attack with a ruby layer explicitly reading it as a curse.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the phonetic technique name and drops the written/reading-layer identification as a curse, weakening what the attack is before it is fired.

findings.highlight: Fight here…? Why does it have to be here? Why does it have to be now? And why do I have to fight against Tohsaka?
findings.evidenceJa: ここで、本気で、戦うだって……？　なんだってこんな所で、なんだってこんな時に、なんだってよりにもよって、あの遠坂と戦わなくっちゃいけないのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou reels at having to fight seriously, here, now, and—with especially cruel improbability—against Tohsaka of all people.
findings.explanation: The English drops 本気で and よりにもよって, removing both the fight’s lethal seriousness and the climax that Tohsaka is the worst or most unlikely person for him to face.

findings.highlight: I’ll think about it when that happens.
findings.evidenceJa: その時はその時よ。
findings.governingReading: Rin dismisses the risk with “if it happens, then it happens”—she will handle the consequence at that time.
findings.explanation: “I’ll think about it” makes her postpone deliberation rather than accept and deal with the contingency, softening her decisiveness.

findings.highlight: She moves her arm and starts the fight.
findings.evidenceJa: 何か八つ当たりじみた宣戦布告をして、遠坂の腕が動いた。
findings.governingReading: After issuing what sounds to Shirou like a declaration of war tinged with displaced frustration, Rin moves her arm.
findings.explanation: The English removes the declaration and 八つ当たり judgment entirely, then reverses the order so arm movement itself begins the fight. This erases Shirou’s recognition that her attack partly resembles emotional lashing out.

findings.highlight: my vision is filled with light.
findings.evidenceJa: 視界が光に潰された。
findings.governingReading: The instant Rin thrusts out her left hand, light crushes or obliterates Shirou’s vision.
findings.explanation: “Filled with light” describes illumination rather than functional blinding, weakening the attack’s immediate disabling effect.

findings.highlight: It’s about four steps forward to the stairs leading to the second floor.
findings.evidenceJa: 二階に続く階段まで、思いっきり飛び込んで四歩。
findings.governingReading: Reaching the stairs to the second floor would require four all-out diving strides.
findings.explanation: The English turns a violently committed escape movement into a neutral approximate distance, losing the speed and physical choice Shirou is calculating.

findings.highlight: it’ll also take me about four steps to get to cover.
findings.evidenceJa: 同じく四歩程度で遠坂の死角に入れる。
findings.governingReading: Returning to the hallway would put Shirou in Rin’s blind spot in roughly four steps.
findings.explanation: “Cover” changes a position outside Rin’s sightline into a physical protective object or sheltered location, altering the tactical basis of the alternative route.

findings.highlight: I don’t know why, but Tohsaka sighs.
findings.evidenceJa: 何がどうしたのか、遠坂は呆れた風に溜息をこぼしてから、
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot tell what prompted it, but Rin visibly sighs in an exasperated or incredulous manner before speaking.
findings.explanation: The English keeps Shirou’s uncertainty but removes the manner of Rin’s sigh, flattening the exasperation that frames her harsh warning.

findings.highlight: Don’t say ridiculous things.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂こそ馬鹿なコト言うなよな。
findings.governingReading: Shirou throws the charge specifically back at Rin: she, of all people, should not say something stupid.
findings.explanation: The English drops こそ’s pointed reversal and softens 馬鹿, removing the tit-for-tat edge of Shirou’s reply to Rin.

findings.highlight: Are there people watching us now?
findings.evidenceJa: じゃあ聞くけど、ここは人目のある所かしら
findings.governingReading: Rin asks whether this is a place exposed to public eyes or witnesses.
findings.explanation: The English changes the location’s general public visibility into whether people are actively watching at that instant, narrowing Rin’s rebuttal to Shirou’s safety rule.

findings.highlight: I can cast any magic carved on here just by filling it with magical energy.
findings.evidenceJa: ここに刻まれた魔術なら、わたしは魔力を通すだけで発動させる事ができる
findings.governingReading: Rin can activate the magecraft engraved in the Crest merely by passing magical energy through it.
findings.explanation: “Carved on here” is malformed and “filling it” replaces energy routed through the Crest with an ambiguous filling action, obscuring the stated activation mechanism.

findings.highlight: It is an ultimate hastening mechanism that runs the car called magic just by turning it on.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ回すだけで魔術という車を走らせる、究極の短縮機関。
findings.governingReading: The Crest is an ultimate abbreviation or shortcut mechanism: simply turn it and the car called magecraft runs.
findings.explanation: “Hastening mechanism” conveys speed rather than the shortening or bypassing of procedures that defines the Crest’s function; “turning it on” also blurs the source’s mechanical metaphor.

findings.highlight: …And besides, I don’t think I can stand having you walk about carelessly.
findings.evidenceJa: ……それに、今日みたいにふらふらされてたらわたしの神経が持ちそうにないし
findings.governingReading: If Shirou keeps wandering around as he did today, Rin doubts her nerves can take it.
findings.explanation: The English omits “like today” and reduces the explicit image of Rin’s nerves failing to generic inability to stand his behavior, weakening the concern beneath her proposed attack.

findings.highlight: This is no time to think. I[line3][lr]
findings.evidenceJa: 戸惑ってる場合じゃない、今は[line4]
findings.governingReading: This is no time to hesitate or remain bewildered; the thought deliberately carries into the next page.
findings.explanation: The English changes hesitation or confusion into thinking and exposes a stray incomplete “I” at the page break, damaging both the mental command and its presentation.
